title: Noise-Tolerant DDoS Detection for Edge Networks
problem: Edge-network defenders need to distinguish hostile traffic under noisy observations and constrained compute budgets.
system: A first-author study of noise-tolerant shallow neural networks for DDoS detection in computational social and edge-network settings.
evaluation: Comparative experimental evaluation is documented in the peer-reviewed IEEE article; this profile does not reproduce unverified headline metrics.
relevance: Resource-aware network monitoring, IoT defense, and security systems that must remain useful when data quality shifts.
imageAlt: Compact diagram of a DDoS traffic and defense workflow

title: Two-Stage LLM-Enhanced DDoS Detection
problem: Next-generation IoT and edge environments need detection pipelines that combine efficient traffic analysis with interpretable, context-aware reasoning.
system: A first-author, two-stage framework presented at IEEE GLOBECOM 2025 that connects DDoS detection with an LLM-enhanced analysis stage.
evaluation: The conference paper reports the experimental protocol and results; this site links to the DOI record without restating unverified figures.
relevance: Security operations, explainable alert triage, and on-premise or resource-conscious network defense workflows.
imageAlt: Conceptual overview of a two-stage LLM-enhanced DDoS detection workflow

title: Foreground-Centric Fine-Grained Recognition
problem: Fine-grained visual classifiers can learn background shortcuts instead of the subtle subject features that distinguish similar categories.
system: A first-author pipeline that centers detected foreground subjects before classification to study robustness in fine-grained bird recognition.
evaluation: The peer-reviewed Signal, Image and Video Processing article compares the foreground-centric approach within a controlled recognition pipeline.
relevance: Visual inspection, biodiversity monitoring, and recognition systems operating across changing environments.
imageAlt: Foreground-centric learning pipeline from source images through subject crops and classification

title: Vision–Language Image Captioning with ViT and GPT-J
problem: Image captioning requires a model to align visual representations with coherent language while retaining relevant scene context.
system: A first-author vision encoder–language decoder study integrating a Vision Transformer with GPT-J for image caption generation.
evaluation: The published AIPR chapter describes training and evaluation on image-caption data using established language-generation measures.
relevance: Accessible visual interfaces, media understanding, and multimodal information systems.
imageAlt: Conceptual image-captioning pipeline connecting a vision encoder to a language decoder
